message.text:
The browser request for another user's profile image reaches the data layer through the fileserver. The trace begins with `serveUserAvatar` looking up the image by username identifier. `GetUserAvatar` remains in ACL but is no longer an active RPC.

`parseDataURI` extracts the stored image bytes from `AvatarURL`. `ListUsers` queries `avatar_url` from the database; SQLite is representative, though MySQL and Postgres follow the same pattern.

`serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go`  
`Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go`  
`DB.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (same method in `store/db/mysql/user.go`, `store/db/postgres/user.go`)

The browser hits `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` (`RegisterRoutes` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`). `convertUserFromStore` in `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` sets that URL for stored data-URI avatars. The lookup is by username, so `GetUser` skips the ID cache and loads via `ListUsers`, which selects `avatar_url`. `serveUserAvatar` then decodes that column with `parseDataURI`.
